profiles.name: Clarke Gordon
profiles.excerpt: Clarke Gordon combined radio acting with later production work, building a career that moved from network drama into film and television.
profiles.bio_html:
Clarke Gordon was born in Detroit in 1918 and developed a career across radio, stage, film and television. His early professional work placed him in the same West Coast dramatic repertory that supplied anthology, detective and science-fiction programs with reliable supporting actors.

Gordon appeared on programs including Lux Radio Theatre, NBC University Theater and X Minus One, then expanded his career into screen work and production. His later credits as a producer make that work a legitimate second professional branch rather than a one-off credit.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Gordon, four each on NBC University Theater and X Minus One, two each on Richard Diamond, Private Detective and The Adventures of Philip Marlowe, plus additional work on Escape, Frontier Gentleman and Gunsmoke.

profiles.name: JoAnne Johnson
profiles.excerpt: JoAnne Johnson gave Danger, Dr. Danfield its continuing female lead as secretary Rusty Fairfax throughout the surviving run of the 1946 crime series.
profiles.bio_html:
JoAnne Johnson is best documented in radio through her continuing role on Danger, Dr. Danfield. She played Rusty Fairfax, secretary to criminal psychologist Dr. Daniel Danfield, and was part of the central two-character relationship that framed each week's investigation.

Rusty did more than receive exposition. The series used her conversations with Danfield to move between the case itself and his reconstruction of the crime, making Johnson's role structurally important to the program's narrative format across its full run.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 25 Danger, Dr. Danfield performances credited to Johnson. Her canonical public name is standardized as JoAnne Johnson while the archive source spelling Joanne Johnson remains preserved.

profiles.name: Kristoffer Tabori
profiles.excerpt: Kristoffer Tabori brought a lifelong acting career into CBS Radio Mystery Theater before becoming an Emmy-winning director and an acclaimed audiobook narrator.
profiles.bio_html:
Kristoffer Tabori was born in Malibu in 1952 into a filmmaking family and began acting while still a child. By his teens he was already working professionally on stage, and he later built a career across theatre, film, television and radio.

Tabori became a recurring performer on CBS Radio Mystery Theater, then developed substantial second careers behind the camera and at the microphone. He directed television films and series, won an Emmy for directing, and became an award-winning audiobook narrator, making direction and narration genuine parts of his professional identity.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 25 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Tabori. Those broadcasts capture the dramatic-radio side of a career that later expanded deeply into directing and long-form narration.

profiles.name: Marlin Hurt
profiles.excerpt: Marlin Hurt was a musician, singer and radio comedian whose Beulah character became nationally famous on Fibber McGee and Molly before receiving a spinoff series.
profiles.bio_html:
Marlin Hurt was born in Illinois in 1905 and worked professionally as a singer, saxophonist and stage entertainer before radio made him nationally known. He sang with Vincent Lopez's orchestra and performed in the vocal trio Tom, Dick and Harry, giving music a substantial place in his career before comedy took over.

Hurt became famous for portraying Beulah, a Black domestic character performed in dialect by a white male actor. The character became a hit on Fibber McGee and Molly and was spun off into The Marlin Hurt and Beulah Show. The role is historically important but also reflects racial caricature conventions that later versions of Beulah moved away from when Black actresses took over the part.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 25 Fibber McGee and Molly performances credited to Hurt. His profile also retains singing and instrumental music as genuine professional branches because both preceded and supported his radio-comedy career.

profiles.name: Yvonne Peattie
profiles.excerpt: Yvonne Peattie was a West Coast radio actress whose surviving work crosses prestige anthology, hard-boiled detective drama and FBI stories before a later film career.
profiles.bio_html:
Yvonne Peattie was born in San Francisco in 1916 and built a professional acting career that included radio, film and television. During World War II she also served with the Red Cross Motor Corps and Blood Bank before returning to entertainment work.

Radio placed Peattie repeatedly in the West Coast dramatic repertory, where she moved between anthology adaptations and detective programs. Her credits include Lux Radio Theatre, Jeff Regan, Investigator, The Adventures of Philip Marlowe and Pat Novak, for Hire, showing a career built on flexible supporting work rather than one continuing character.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves eight Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Peattie, six Jeff Regan, Investigator appearances, three The Adventures of Philip Marlowe episodes, two each on Pat Novak, for Hire and Richard Diamond, Private Detective, plus additional work on This Is Your FBI.

profiles.name: Alec Harford
profiles.excerpt: Alec Harford brought decades of British stage and screen experience to American radio, where he became a dependable player in literary and suspense drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Alec Harford was born in London in 1888 and built a long acting career in Britain and the United States. By the time he became a regular presence in American radio drama, he already had decades of stage and screen experience behind him.

Harford's mature voice made him especially useful in literary adaptations and suspense. He worked repeatedly on NBC University Theater and Escape, where supporting actors often had to establish period, class and character in only a few lines while carrying dense dramatic material.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 11 NBC University Theater performances credited to Harford, eight Escape appearances, four Lux Radio Theatre broadcasts and an additional Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar performance.

profiles.name: Amzie Strickland
profiles.excerpt: Amzie Strickland began in radio and sustained one of the longest careers in American character acting, moving through thousands of broadcasts and hundreds of television appearances.
profiles.bio_html:
Amzie Strickland was born in Oklahoma City in 1919 and began professional acting while still young. Radio became an important early foundation, with continuing roles in programs such as Call the Police, The Fat Man, Our Gal Sunday and The Romance of Helen Trent.

Strickland carried that repertory experience into an exceptionally long screen career, eventually appearing in hundreds of television episodes while continuing film and commercial work. Her radio background helps explain the ease with which she moved among sharply different supporting characters for decades.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves eight The Shadow performances credited to Strickland, two each on Barrie Craig, CBS Radio Mystery Theater, Gang Busters, Inner Sanctum Mysteries and The Chase, plus additional appearances on Suspense and The Falcon.

profiles.name: Bob Martin
profiles.excerpt: Bob Martin was one of the young actors who played Dan Reid, the nephew of the Lone Ranger, in the long-running WXYZ adventure series.
profiles.bio_html:
Bob Martin is best documented in radio as one of the child and juvenile performers who played Dan Reid, nephew of the Lone Ranger. The role placed him inside the continuing family mythology of one of American radio's most successful adventure serials.

Dan Reid was more than an occasional child character. His connection to the Ranger and to later Green Hornet family lore made the part part of the wider fictional history created around the WXYZ programs. Martin shared the role across the years with other young actors as the character aged and production needs changed.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 24 The Lone Ranger performances credited to Martin. Those broadcasts provide the clearest surviving record of his contribution to the series and to the Dan Reid character.

profiles.name: Clarence Hartzell
profiles.excerpt: Clarence Hartzell combined music and comic character acting, creating memorable elderly voices on Vic and Sade and Lum and Abner.
profiles.bio_html:
Clarence Hartzell developed as both a musician and comic actor before becoming one of radio's recognizable elderly-character specialists. His voice could suggest a rambling small-town eccentric with such conviction that listeners often assumed the performer himself was much older than he was.

Hartzell became well known as Uncle Fletcher on Vic and Sade and later joined Lum and Abner as Benjamin Franklin Withers. Contemporary trade coverage records his arrival on the series in 1948, while later histories also note the musical side of his professional life, making instrumental performance a legitimate second facet.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 24 Lum and Abner performances credited to Hartzell. Those broadcasts capture the Pine Ridge character work that became one of the strongest surviving parts of his radio career.

profiles.name: Marian Richman
profiles.excerpt: Marian Richman was a versatile West Coast radio actress whose surviving work ranges from literary adaptations and westerns to detective and suspense drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Marian Richman belongs to the busy supporting repertory of postwar radio, where professional actors moved among anthology productions, westerns, crime stories and musical programs. Personal biographical detail is limited, but her cast record shows steady work across several major network series.

Richman's credits include NBC University Theater, Wild Bill Hickok, Escape, Rocky Fortune and Tales of the Texas Rangers. The variety of those programs reflects a performer hired for range rather than identified with one continuing character.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six NBC University Theater performances credited to Richman, five Wild Bill Hickok appearances, two each on Escape, Rocky Fortune, Tales of the Texas Rangers and The Railroad Hour, plus additional work on Broadway Is My Beat and CBS Radio Workshop.
